words.gram: n. acc. sg. (bahuvrīhi, f. acc. sg.)

hindi: कृश और प्रसन्न मुख वाली, फड़कते हुए श्रोणि यानी कूल्हों और स्तनों वाली
english: (A woman) with a lean, clear face, and with throbbing hips and breasts,
notes: Accusative feminine bahuvrīhi, the object of 'vidyāt' in unit 88. GROUPING: this unit appears to continue in 88. 'payodhara' (lit. 'water-bearer') = breast (standard). 'śroṇi' = hip/pelvic region (standard). Printed fused 'sphuracchroṇi' read as sphurat+śroṇi (ch- from sandhi).

words.gram: m. acc. sg. (bahuvrīhi, f. acc. sg.)

words.gloss: a woman in her fertile season (ṛtumatī)

hindi: जिस स्त्री की आँखें और कुक्षि शिथिल हों और जिसे पुरुष की कामना हो, उसे ऋतुमती स्त्री जानना चाहिए।
english: One should know that woman to be in her fertile season (ṛtumatī) who has drooping eyes and belly and desire for a man.

text_flags.why: possible: 'akṣu' is not a word; 'akṣi' (eye) is the expected member
possible: accusative feminine expected to agree with 'striyam'; final anusvāra apparently dropped

notes: GROUPING: continues 87 (the accusative descriptions in 87 and here qualify 'striyam'). 'kukṣi' = belly/flank. 'ṛtumatī' = a woman in the ṛtu (her fertile period after menstruation) (standard sense).

hindi: जैसे दिन बीत जाने पर कमल संकोच को प्राप्त होता है, वैसे ही
english: As a lotus comes to contraction when the day has passed, so
notes: GROUPING: the comparison is completed in 90 ('yoniḥ sā ...'). 'dine atīte' locative absolute.

hindi: ऋतुकाल बीत जाने पर वह योनि भीतर शुक्र को ग्रहण नहीं करती।
english: when the fertile season (ṛtu) has passed, that yoni (womb) does not receive semen (śukra) inside.

text_flags.why: possible: 'kṛtāvatīte' is not a sensible compound; ṛtau atīte (when the ṛtu is past) fits the sense and the comparison with the lotus after the day has passed; initial k- probably an added or misread letter

notes: Completes the comparison of 89. 'yoni' = womb / female genital passage (probable; the exact organ is not specified by the word). The restored 'ṛtau atīte' rests on one conjectured letter.

words.gloss: by a month, over a month

hindi: एक मास में संचित रक्त को, ऋतुकाल में फिर, दो धमनियों द्वारा
english: Blood accumulated over a month, again in the fertile season (ṛtu), by the two dhamanīs (vessels),
notes: GROUPING: the sentence is completed in 92 (verb 'sṛdet'). 'upacitaṃ raktaṃ' agree. dhamanī = a vessel or channel (probable; whether artery, vein or other duct is not stated); two are named. The exact case sense of 'dhamanībhyām' (instrumental dual) is by means of the two vessels.

words.gloss: from the mouth of the yoni

hindi: थोड़ा काला और दुर्गन्ध वाला रक्त वायु योनि के मुख से बाहर निकालता है।
english: slightly dark and ill-smelling, wind (vāyu) would discharge from the mouth of the yoni.

text_flags.why: possible: 'sṛdet' is not a verb form; opt. 3 sg. of √sṛj 'send out' fits the sense (d for j is a common OCR/print confusion)

notes: Completes 91: the object is the blood (raktam) of 91. This unit is the verb phrase of that sentence. Hindi uses the plain present for the optative.

words.gloss: at the sight of the flower (puṣpa), i.e. menstruation
sleeping on a spread of darbha grass

hindi: तब पुष्पदर्शन यानी रजोदर्शन होने पर पहले दिन से ही स्त्री ब्रह्मचारिणी रहे, स्नान और अलंकार से रहित, दर्भ के बिछौने पर सोती हुई, तीन रात तक रहे।
english: Then, when the flower is seen (puṣpadarśana: the onset of menstruation), from the first day onward she should remain a chaste woman (brahmacāriṇī), without bathing and ornaments, sleeping on a spread of darbha grass, for three nights.
notes: Prose unit; the subject (the woman, 'strī') is not named and is understood from the context. 'puṣpa' (flower) is the usual word for the menstrual flow; 'puṣpadarśana' = first sight of menses (standard). 'āsīta' is 'should stay / sit', here 'remain'.

hindi: और पत्ते के दोने या हथेली, इनमें से किसी एक में, दूध के साथ पकाया हुआ थोड़ा यावक यानी सम्भवतः जौ से बना एक पदार्थ, कृश करने के लिए खाए।
english: And, in one of the two, a leaf-bowl or the palm of the hand, she should eat a little yāvaka (probably a barley preparation) cooked with milk, for the purpose of thinning (karśana).

text_flags.why: possible: two words printed joined without a space; no letter changed

notes: 'yāvaka' is probably a preparation of yava, barley (probable); the word can also mean lac, but that does not suit eating. 'anyatame' with the two nouns is taken as 'in either one of the two'. Subject (the woman of 93) is understood. 'karśana' = making lean/thin.

hindi: तीखे, गरम, खट्टे और नमकीन को त्याग दे।
english: She should avoid sharp, hot, sour and salty (ones).
notes: Subject (the woman of 93) and the nouns (food) are understood. The compound is a dvandva of four qualities; 'tīkṣṇa' = sharp/pungent.

words.gram: ppp. caus. f. nom. sg. ud-√vṛt

words.gloss: with auspicious rites and benedictions performed
with the mind on no other

hindi: चौथे दिन उबटन लगाई हुई, ठण्डे जल से नहाई हुई, लेप लगाई हुई, अलंकृत, श्वेत माला और वस्त्र वाली, मंगल और स्वस्त्ययन किए हुए, अन्य किसी में मन न रखने वाली स्त्री ठीक इसी प्रकार के पति को देखे।
english: On the fourth day, rubbed with unguent powder, bathed in cold water, anointed, adorned, wearing white garlands and garments, with auspicious rites and benedictions performed, with her mind on no other, she should look upon a husband of just this kind.

text_flags.why: possible: three words printed fused; final -ā + e- sandhi gives -ai-; no letter wrong

notes: Subject (the woman of 93) understood. 'evaṃvidha' (of this kind) refers back to a description not in this unit; the husband's qualities are not stated here. 'udvartitā' from udvartana, rubbing with powder (probable sense).

hindi: क्योंकि उस समय वह जिस प्रकार के को ही देखती या सोचती है, वैसे को ही जन्म देती है।
english: For then, whatever kind (of one) she sees or thinks of, a (one) of that kind she bears.
notes: Objects are unstated ('yādṛśam', 'tādṛśam' are adjectives); the sense is the kind of person seen or thought of, and a like child. Closing 'iti' marks the end of the statement; not translated.

words.gloss: desiring a son with good qualities

hindi: तब स्नान के बाद, फिर भी, गुणवान् पुत्र की इच्छा वाला चार रात छोड़ दे।
english: Then, after the bath, again, one desiring a son with good qualities should let four nights pass.

text_flags.why: possible: an anusvāra before t- is the print's usual way of writing n; here the ablative -āt is meant
possible: long ū is not expected in catur-rātra (four nights)

notes: 'upekṣeta' (look over, disregard, let pass) is read as letting four nights go by; this is a conjectural sense in context (counting with 99-100 reaches the 8th night). The subject is not stated: 'putrārthī' is masculine, but the form is the general one. 'snātāt' (ablative of snāta, 'after the bath') is an unusual form. GROUPING: this unit appears to continue with 99 and 100.

words.gloss: from the day of the flower, i.e. of menstruation

hindi: पुष्प के दिन से सात रात
english: From the day of the flower (menstruation), seven nights.

text_flags.why: possible: 'puṣpe-' with locative -e is awkward inside a compound; 'puṣpa-dināt' fits the sense; the alternative is the two words puṣpe dināt

notes: Fragment without a verb; GROUPING: appears to belong with 98 (the nights to let pass) and to lead on to 100. No verb is supplied.

hindi: फिर आठवीं, दसवीं अथवा बारहवीं रात में पुत्र की कामना वाला सहवास करे।
english: Then, on the eighth, tenth or twelfth night, one desiring a son should lie together.
notes: 'rātrau' is singular and understood with each ordinal. The object of 'saṃviśet' is not stated.

hindi: अथवा पाँचवीं, सातवीं या नवीं रात में पुत्री की कामना वाला।
english: Or on the fifth, seventh or ninth (night), one desiring a daughter.
notes: Elliptic: the verb 'saṃviśet' and the word 'rātrau' are carried from unit 100; no verb is supplied in the translation. GROUPING: this unit appears to continue 100.

words.gloss: in progressive order, each later one more

hindi: उन रातों में उत्तरोत्तर सन्तान को आयु, आरोग्य, ऐश्वर्य, सौभाग्य, बल, वर्ण यानी रंग और इन्द्रियों की सम्पदा प्राप्त होती है।
english: In these (nights), progressively, the offspring has the endowment of life-span, health, lordship, good fortune, strength, complexion (varṇa) and the sense faculties.
notes: 'apatyasya bhavati' is a genitive of possession ('there is to the offspring'). 'saṃpad' is read as the last member of one long dvandva-plus compound, 'endowment of' the whole list. 'varṇa' = complexion (probable; it can also mean colour or class).

hindi: किन्तु इसके आगे तो आयु आदि का उत्तरोत्तर ही ह्रास होता है।
english: But after this there is a progressive decrease of life-span and the rest.
notes: Copula understood. 'ādi' = 'and the rest', that is the list in 102. GROUPING: follows 102.

words.gloss: ārtava (menstrual blood, the female generative fluid; standard)

hindi: उनमें सम रात्रियों में आर्तव यानी मासिक रक्तस्राव अल्प हो जाता है और विषम रात्रियों में बढ़ता है।
english: Among these, in the even nights the ārtava (menstrual blood) becomes small; in the odd (ones) it increases.
notes: 'rātriṣu' is understood with 'ayugmāsu'. ārtava = menstrual blood / female generative fluid (standard). The subject of 'āpyāyate' is the same ārtava.

hindi: इसलिए उन रात्रियों में क्रम से पुत्र का और पुत्री का जन्म होता है।
english: Therefore in these (nights), in order, there is the birth of a son and of a daughter.
notes: Copula understood. 'kramāt' = in the order (even/odd) of the nights; the pairing 'son : even / daughter : odd' is not spelled out in this unit. 'tāsu' refers back to the nights of 100-104.

words.gloss: one in whom the sight of ārtava has not ceased

hindi: और इसीलिए जिस स्त्री का आर्तव दिखना बन्द नहीं हुआ है, उसके पास पुत्र की इच्छा वाला विषम दिनों में भी न जाए।
english: And for this very reason one desiring a son should not approach a woman in whom the sight of the ārtava (menstrual blood) has not ceased, even on odd days.
notes: The woman is the bahuvrīhi in the accusative, 'one whose seeing of ārtava has not stopped'. 'ahassu' is a printed variant of ahaḥsu. The unit speaks of days, the earlier ones of nights; the text is followed as printed.

hindi: किन्तु यदि आहार के अनुसार विषम रात्रियों में शुक्र की अधिकता और सम रात्रियों में कमी हो, तब पुरुष स्त्री के आकार वाला, दुर्बल या हीन अंगों वाला उत्पन्न होता है।
english: But if, owing to conformity to diet, there is an abundance of semen (śukra) in the odd (nights) and a deficiency in the even ones, then a male is born of female form, weak, or deficient in limb.

text_flags.why: possible: two words printed fused; no letter changed

notes: 'āhāra-anurodha' is read as 'conformity to / following the diet'; the sense of the cause is not fully clear. 'rātriṣu' understood with ayugmāsu, yugmāsu. 'tataḥpumān' is printed fused (tataḥ pumān).

hindi: और स्त्री पुरुष के आकार वाली, दुर्बल या हीन अंगों वाली।
english: And a female of male form, weak, or deficient in limb.
notes: Elliptic: the verb 'jāyate' is carried from 107 and not supplied. GROUPING: continues 107. 'durbalāhīnāṃgī' is printed fused (durbalā hīnāṅgī); no letter wrong.

words.gloss: napuṃsaka (a person who is neither male nor female; eunuch, impotent; standard)

hindi: किन्तु ग्यारहवीं और तेरहवीं रात में नपुंसक होगा।
english: But on the eleventh and thirteenth (nights) there would be a napuṃsaka (a person neither male nor female; eunuch).
notes: 'rātriṣu' understood. 'napuṃsaka' (lit. 'non-male') also is the grammatical term for neuter; here a person is meant. The Hindi word नपुंसक covers impotent and eunuch, as does the Sanskrit.

words.gloss: relating to a son, for obtaining a son

hindi: तब उपाध्याय यानी आचार्य पुत्र सम्बन्धी विधान का आचरण करे।
english: Then the teacher (upādhyāya) should perform the procedure relating to a son (putrīya).
notes: 'putrīya' is the adjective 'relating to a son'. The rite itself is not described in this unit; the 'upādhyāya' is a teacher/preceptor (probable; he may act as the officiating priest).

hindi: किन्तु शुद्ध हुई स्त्री के लिए मन्त्र से रहित।
english: But for the purified woman, devoid of mantra.

text_flags.why: possible: a neuter -m ending may have been lost; read as 'mantra-varjitam', but the printed form is also usable as a stem

notes: Fragment with no verb and no stated noun; the sense is probably that the procedure for the purified woman is without a mantra (conjectural). 'śuddhā' = purified (apparently after the bath of 96). GROUPING: appears to belong with 110 (the procedure), unclear how.

words.gloss: having the form, complexion and conduct of that (son)

hindi: और जिस प्रकार के पुत्र की वह आशा करे, उसके रूप, वर्ण और आचरण वाले जनपदों का चिन्तन करो, इस प्रकार स्त्री से कहना चाहिए।
english: And the woman is to be told: 'Think upon the janapadas (regions or their peoples) that have the form, complexion and conduct of whatever kind of son you may wish for.'
notes: 'janapada' = a region or its people (standard); both senses are possible. The 'iti' closes the quoted instruction. The 'tad' in the compound refers to the wished-for son.

hindi: और उस जनपद के आहार, विहार, उपचार और परिच्छद का अनुसरण करे।
english: And she should follow the food, way of living (vihāra), practices (upacāra) and accessories (paricchada) of that region.
notes: The printed whole is one fused token; it is read as dvandva 'āhāra-vihāra-upacāra-paricchada' attached to 'tad-janapada', then 'ca' and the verb. The English glosses for vihāra, upacāra and paricchada are the plainest senses; each has others (e.g. upacāra = treatment / service; paricchada = retinue, apparel). Subject (the woman) understood from 112.

words.gloss: at the end of the rite (karman)
in a part of the night

hindi: और रीति पूरी होने पर पुरुष एक मास ब्रह्मचारी रहकर, घी और दूध के साथ शालि का भात खाकर, अधिक न खाया हुआ, सुखी, माला पहने, प्रसन्न मन वाला, तृप्त अंगों वाला, श्वेत वस्त्र पहने, मुहूर्त जानने वाले को मान्य रात्रि के भाग में, कल्याणकारी बातें सोचता हुआ, उसकी कामना वाला, भली-भाँति बिछी शय्या पर दाहिने पैर से पूर्व की ओर चढ़े।
english: And at the end of the rite, the man, chaste for a month, having eaten boiled śāli rice with ghee and milk, not over-fed, happy, wearing a garland, cheerful, with limbs refreshed, in white clothes, in a part of the night approved by the muhūrta-expert (astrologer), thinking of auspicious things, desirous of that, should mount the well-spread bed with the right foot, toward the east.

text_flags.why: possible: 'karmāte' is not a word; anusvāra/n lost before t (karma-anta)
possible: 'abhiprāiya' is not a form; the gerund of abhi-pra-√aś 'having eaten' fits (ś misread as i)
possible: only the anusvāra spelling of ṅ; no change in sense

notes: Long single prose sentence with one main verb 'ārohet' (should mount). 'prāk' can mean 'toward the east' or 'first, forward'; the parallel 115 uses 'pūrvam' for 'first', so 'east' is taken. 'karmānta' (end of the rite) is taken from the corrected reading and its object rite is not named here. 'mauhūrtika' = one skilled in muhūrta (timing); astrologer (standard). 'śāli' = a kind of rice (Oryza sativa, standard) and 'odana' = boiled rice. 'tad-abhikāma' = desiring 'that' (the union), literal. 'ca' in 'karmāte ca' is read as 'and'. Subject: the man.

words.gloss: with oil and māṣa (black gram) as the chief food

hindi: उसी प्रकार की स्त्री, कृश अंगों वाली, तेल और माष यानी उड़द प्रधान आहार वाली, पहले बाएँ पैर से पुरुष के दाहिनी ओर शय्या पर चढ़े।
english: And the woman, likewise prepared, with limbs made thin and with oil and māṣa (black gram) as the chief food, should first ascend the bed with the left foot, on the right of the man.

text_flags.why: possible: two words printed fused; no letter changed

notes: 'tad-vidhā eva' = of just that kind, i.e. prepared in the same way as the man. 'uttara' in 'uttarāhāra' = chief or additional/following: here 'chief' is taken (conjectural). māṣa = black gram, Vigna mungo (standard). 'dakṣiṇataḥ' is taken with 'puruṣasya' as 'on the man's right'.

hindi: वहाँ मन्त्र का प्रयोग करे।
english: There one should employ the mantra.
notes: The subject is not stated; the man is probably meant (conjectural). The mantra is given in 117.

words.gloss: ahi (serpent; sense in the mantra unclear)

hindi: तुम अहि हो, तुम आयु हो, तुम सब ओर प्रतिष्ठा यानी आधार हो। धाता तुम्हें स्थापित करे, विधाता तुम्हें स्थापित करे। ब्रह्मवर्चस से युक्त होओ।
english: You are the ahi; you are life; you are the support on every side. May Dhātṛ place you; may Vidhātṛ place you. Be one with brahma-splendour (brahmavarcas).

text_flags.why: possible: the mantra is elsewhere read 'ahir asi'; the long ā looks like a print or transcription slip

notes: This is the mantra announced in 116. The sense of 'ahi' here is unclear (serpent is the plain meaning; the word is kept). 'dadhātu' has no stated object in the Sanskrit beyond 'tvā'. 'brahmavarcasā bhava' = 'be with brahmavarcas'. Closing 'iti' ends the mantra and is not translated.

hindi: ब्रह्मा, बृहस्पति, विष्णु, सोम, सूर्य तथा दोनों अश्विनौ,
english: Brahmā, Bṛhaspati, Viṣṇu, Soma, Sūrya, and also the two Aśvins,
notes: A list of deities, the subject of 'dadhatu' in 119. GROUPING: appears to continue 117 (the mantra) and to be completed by 119.

hindi: भग, फिर मित्र और वरुण, मुझे वीर पुत्र प्रदान करें।
english: Bhaga, and then Mitra and Varuṇa: may they bestow on me a heroic son.
notes: Completes the list begun in 118; the subject of 'dadhatu' is the deities named in 118-119 (appears to continue 118). 'me' is taken as 'for me'. Closing 'iti' ends the mantra and is not translated.

hindi: तब परस्पर मधुर वचनों से सान्त्वना देकर, हर्ष के साथ, अनुकूल रीति से दोनों सहवास करें।
english: Then, having soothed each other with gentle words, they two should lie together, with joy and agreeably.

text_flags.why: possible: 'saṃvesetām' is not a regular form; the dual optative of sam-√viś (cf. 'saṃviśet' in 100) is meant

notes: 'sāman' here means conciliatory or gentle speech (probable; it can also be a Vedic chant). The dual shows both partners are the subject.

hindi: और अन्त में इसे अचानक ठण्डे जल से सींचे।
english: And at the end he should suddenly sprinkle her with cold water.

text_flags.why: possible: 'paryānta' with long ā is not the usual form (paryanta)
possible: long ā in the prefix pari- is not expected

notes: The subject is not stated; the man is understood (conjectural). 'enām' refers to the woman.

hindi: इस विषय में, अधिक खाई हुई, भूखी, प्यासी, डरी हुई, उदास मन वाली, शोक से पीड़ित, क्रोधित, अत्यन्त स्थूल, किसी दूसरे की कामना वाली अथवा सहवास की इच्छा न रखने वाली स्त्री गर्भ धारण नहीं करती, या दोषयुक्त गर्भ धारण करती है।
english: In this matter, a woman who is over-fed, hungry, thirsty, frightened, dejected, afflicted by grief, angry, very fat, desiring another, or desiring no intercourse, does not bear a foetus (garbha), or bears a defective one.

text_flags.why: possible: final anusvāra lost; accusative singular expected as object of 'dhatte'

notes: 'atimedurā' is read as 'very fat / very unctuous' (probable; medura = smooth, fatty). 'avyavāya' = absence of intercourse (vyavāya = sexual union, standard). 'viguṇa' = faulty, defective. The two 'vā' join the list members and the two outcomes.

hindi: इसी प्रकार पुरुष भी; और वह नीचे न रहे।
english: Likewise the man also; and he should not stay below.
notes: The first clause has no verb. The sense is probably that the man too should not be in the states listed in 122 (conjectural); no verb is supplied. 'adhaḥ' = below, that is, under the woman (probable).

hindi: क्योंकि इस प्रकार स्त्री की चेष्टा वाला पुरुष उत्पन्न होता है, अथवा पुरुष की चेष्टा वाली स्त्री।
english: For thus a male is born with a woman's behaviour, or a female with a man's behaviour.
notes: Gives the stated result of the man staying below in 123 (the link 'tathā hi' = 'for thus'). GROUPING: follows 123.

hindi: और औंधी पड़ी हुई अथवा करवट पर पड़ी हुई स्त्री का सेवन न करे।
english: And one should not resort to a woman lying face down or lying on her side.
notes: 'nyubja' (also nyubja = face down) is the usual form. 'seveta' = resort to, have union with; the object (the woman) is the accusative feminine. The subject is not stated (the man is probably meant).

hindi: औंधी पड़ी हुई स्त्री में वात बलवान है; वह योनि को पीड़ित करता है।
english: In one lying face down Vāta is strong; it presses upon the yoni (womb).
notes: Vāta is one of the three doṣas (kept, no modern equivalent). 'yoni' is the female genital passage/womb (probable). Copula understood in the first clause.

words.gloss: of one lying on the right side

hindi: दाहिनी करवट पर पड़ी हुई स्त्री का श्लेष्मा यानी कफ दबकर अपने स्थान से हटा हुआ गर्भाशय को ढक देता है।
english: In one lying on the right side, Kapha (śleṣman), pressed and displaced, closes the womb (garbhāśaya).
notes: 'śleṣman' = Kapha (standard synonym). 'garbhāśaya' = womb/uterus (standard). 'cyuta' = fallen away from its place. 'apidadhāti' can be 'covers' or 'closes up'; the plainer 'closes' is used.

words.gloss: of one lying on the left side

hindi: बायीं करवट पर पड़ी हुई स्त्री का पित्त उसी प्रकार रक्त और शुक्र को जलाता है।
english: In one lying on the left side, similarly Pitta scorches the blood (rakta) and the semen (śukra).

text_flags.why: possible: 'śuke' is not a word; the neuter dual 'rakta-śukre' (blood and semen) fits sense and metre

notes: 'vi-dah' = burns up, scorches (rakta-śukre as dual objects). 'tadvat' = similarly to 126-127. Pitta is a doṣa (kept).

hindi: इसलिए चित लेटी हुई स्त्री बीज को ग्रहण करे।
english: Therefore, lying on her back, she should receive the seed (bīja, semen).

text_flags.why: likely: 'dasmāt' is not a word; t misprinted d (ta/da confusion)

notes: 'bīja' = seed, here semen (probable). The subject is the woman (f. nom. uttānā).
